intro: If you're in central Prachinburi for business or an overnight stop and want a clean, spacious room on a few-hundred-baht budget — Peamsuk Sweet Prachin Buri is a name budget travellers keep coming back to. It's a 2-star hotel on Prachin Road, Na Muang, opened in 2020. The draw is its town-centre location about 170 m from the night market, plus rooms that real reviews praise as bigger than expected, with cold air-con and generous free parking. Rates start at about ฿490/night, rising to roughly ฿700–800 for king rooms or triple rooms.

body.html: The heart of Peamsuk Sweet is a central Prachinburi location at a few-hundred-baht price. The hotel sits on Prachin Road, Na Muang, just about 170 m from the Prachinburi night market — an easy evening stroll for dinner. Convenience stores, a laundry and several restaurants are all within walking distance, and the town centre is only around 490 m away. For anyone here on business, official errands or an overnight stop on the road, that's far more convenient than a hillside resort you'd have to drive to.

The property itself is a simple town-hotel building that opened in 2020. There are around 36 rooms split into twin rooms (Standard Twin), king rooms (Superior King), deluxe doubles and triple rooms (Deluxe Triple). Rooms come with air-con, a fridge, a kettle, a desk, a cable flat-screen TV and a private balcony. What real reviews agree on is that the rooms feel bigger than expected for the price, the air-con runs cold, and the beds are comfortable — solid value on a budget.
"Big room, cold AC, friendly staff, plenty of parking, right in town within walking distance of the market — for this price it's great value for an overnight stay."

Facilities are about what you'd expect at this level. There's generous free parking, a 24-hour front desk and a laundry service, plus a restaurant, a shared lounge and a sitting terrace. The thing to know is that there's no breakfast and no pool — normal for a budget town hotel. In the morning you can walk out to the market or the local rice-and-curry shops nearby, which are only a short distance away.

The town-centre spot is also handy for onward trips. It's about a 15-minute drive to Abhaibhubejhr Hospital and its Thai traditional-medicine museum, Prachinburi's signature landmark. It's close to the Prachinburi National Museum and the City Pillar Shrine, and from here you can drive on toward the Prachinburi side of Khao Yai, the Noen Hom area, or Kabin Buri. If you use it as a one-night base before moving on, it all plans out nicely on a light budget.

To be straight about what to expect: this is a budget 2-star hotel, not a smart property. Some reviews note that a few staff are a little flat rather than warm, and a handful of guests have reported insects such as cockroaches in the room. The decor is plain and to-the-price, with nothing flashy. If you're after polish or a full nature setting, this isn't it — but for a few-hundred-baht room in the middle of town, it gives you space and a location well above its price.

Overall, Peamsuk Sweet earns 8.1 from 22 Trip.com reviews, scoring well for its in-town location and value. Rates start around ฿490 for a standard room, rising to roughly ฿700–800 for king or triple rooms. If you want an in-town room that's spacious, walking distance to the market and easy to park at, on a modest budget, this delivers exactly that for an overnight stay or a business trip in town.

A tip from following the reviews here: if you want a quiet room, ask for an upper floor or one away from the road, and give the room a quick cleanliness check on arrival since it's a budget place. If you're here for the food, walk to the night market in the evening — it's only about 170 m away. Book ahead on long weekends, because cheap in-town rooms like this fill up fast.

honestSummary: Peamsuk Sweet is a sound pick for anyone who wants a spacious, in-town Prachinburi room within walking distance of the market on a few-hundred-baht budget — a 2-star budget hotel with rooms larger than the price suggests, cold air-con and generous free parking, ideal for business in town or an overnight stop on the road. The trade-offs are plain, to-the-price decor, no breakfast or pool, and cleanliness worth checking on arrival.
